title: Same-index coherent scalarReduction for every normalized scalar model
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with embedding $\iota:E\to L$, a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and an integral derived-complete constructible object $A\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $R_E=\varprojlim_m(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_W$ on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $A_{E,m}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_W$, $B_m=(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m)_W$, $B_{L/E}$ for the completed scalar extension with its same-index coefficient maps $A_{E,m}\to B_m$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $R_E,R_L$ also for derived coherent reduction to quotient systems [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Let $S_Y$ be any normalized primitive scalar model for $E\to L$ on $W$, in the prime/finite-field/embedding/scheme setting of [lem-trf-primitive-quotient-scalar-model-existence], and use the coefficient-extension reduction model of [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model]. Then the coherent comparison
$$\operatorname{scalarReduction}_{S_Y}(A):R_L(B_{L/E}A)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{E,L}(A)$$
obtained by applying $R_L$ to the realization isomorphism of $S_Y$ and then the coherent counit is invertible, where $C_{E,L}(A)$ is the normalized [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] coherent $\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1}$-system whose $n$th term is $A\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1})$. Under the tower-data identification of [def-pur-scalar-extension-tower-data], this is the same coherent-reduction isomorphism $\gamma_A:R_L(B_{L/E}A)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{L/E}(R_EA)$. Let $P\to A$ be a flat-term K-flat representative over $R_E$. For every $n\geq0$, its component is the coherent counit induced by
$$(P\otimes_{R_E}A_{E,n+1})\otimes_{A_{E,n+1}}B_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\ (x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab\ }P\otimes_{R_E}B_{n+1},$$
so both source and target use the quotient $B_{n+1}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1}$ at the same index $n$. There is no replacement of $n$ by $e(L/E)n$; ramification is already in the recorded quotient map.

source.place: Coefficient-extension reduction model and normalized primitive scalar model: same-index coherent counit and tower identification

proof.text: Fix the normalized primitive scalar model S_Y and a flat-term K-flat representative P -> A. The effective comparison-model statement supplies the scalar realization with the representative normalization and a canonical coherent quotient presentation for every such P; its statement also says that the counit on the normalized scalar-change system of a constructible derived-complete input is an isomorphism. Applying the coherent reduction functor R_L to the realization isomorphism therefore gives an isomorphism, and composing with that coherent counit gives the invertible scalarReduction_{S_Y}(A). The target is the normalized system C(P) whose terms are the derived tensors with B_{n+1}, so the effectivity counit here is the counit for this same target system, rather than an unrelated finite evaluation.

source.place: The normalized tower reconstruction gives the scalar-extension object, and the comparison is obtained from coherent maps of towers; the argument uses coherent towers rather than only termwise isomorphism classes.

proof.text: For this P, the association maps a_m:(P tensor A_{E,m}) tensor_{A_{E,m}} B_m -> P tensor B_m, together with the actual quotient transitions, satisfy the coefficient-reduction-presentation equations. The transpose-normalization node identifies the composite of the arbitrary normalized realization with the reduction/realization counit with the canonical coefficient-extension comparison: both have the same double transpose, namely the localized strict tensor-unit map determined by the a_m, and the two adjunction transpose bijections are injective. Thus scalarReduction_{S_Y}(A) equals the canonical coherent counit comparison as an entire quotient-system morphism before evaluating any level.

source.place: Existence and uniqueness: the comparison is the unique transpose under the relevant adjunction; naturality and equality follow by uniqueness of transposes.

proof.text: The canonical coefficient-extension comparison is the coherent counit followed by the inverse of the simultaneous scalar-association map, so at level n it is (P tensor A_{E,n+1}) tensor_{A_{E,n+1}} B_{n+1} -> P tensor B_{n+1}, sending (x tensor a) tensor b to x tensor ab. The scalar-extension definition gives the actual maps A_{E,n+1} -> B_{n+1} and their commuting transitions, while the reduction-tower definition gives the actual quotient transitions. Consequently both source and target use B_{n+1} at the same index n; ramification changes the quotient homomorphism and does not introduce e(L/E)n reindexing.

source.place: The scalar-extension comparison is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, and the scalar associator is the displayed map; the comparison is compatible with finite quotients and coherent towers.

proof.text: The tower-data definition names the scalar reduction comparison by applying coherent reduction to the realization and then its counit. Under the tower-data identification in the item, this canonical whole-system comparison is gamma_A. Step 2 identifies the arbitrary normalized-model composite with the same canonical comparison, so scalarReduction_{S_Y}(A)=gamma_A as coherent morphisms, including every transition; the explicit component from step 3 is therefore the n-th component of gamma_A.

source.place: The natural comparison is defined as the transpose under the pullback/direct-image adjunction; the same transpose argument identifies the named comparison at the level of the whole derived system.

proof_origin.place: Scalar-extension comparisons are transposes of scalar-extended evaluation; the tensor associator gives the same transpose, and uniqueness identifies the arbitrary normalized model with the canonical coherent counit.
